newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka privatisation head resigns - official.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka privatisation head resigns - official.

text.p: Sri Lankan Treasury Secretary B.C. Perera confirmed on Wednesday reports that the head of the island's privatisation outfit, Rajan Asirwatham, has resigned.
"Mr. Asiriwatham has resigned," Perera told Reuters.
Newspapers said on Sunday that Asirwatham, chairman of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), had tendered his resignation to President Chandrika Kumaratunga who is also finance minister.
Asirwatham, who earlier declined to comment on the reports, was not immediately available for comment on Wednesday.
Perera said Asirwatham would be replaced by Dr.P.B. Jayesundera, one of the two deputy secretaries to the Treasury.
Independent analysts said Jayesundera would only stay on till the government finds a permanent replacement for Asirwatham.
PERC was set up in 1995 as a presidential task force to advice the government on privatisation and the restructuring of loss making state sector enterprises.
It was converted to a statutory body responsible to parliament in January last year.
PERC had been criticised in recent months for its handling of the sale of the government gas distribution monopoly to a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
